Series::logit¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::logit(double eps) const -> Series
Series& Series::logit_(double eps)

What It Does¶

logit() is the inverse of sigmoid() — it maps a probability in (0, 1) back to the real-valued score that produced it:

logit(p) = log(p / (1 - p))

p = 0.5 maps to 0, p above 0.5 to a positive score, p below 0.5 to a negative one, and the mapping is antisymmetric: logit(p) = -logit(1 - p). As p approaches 0 or 1 the output diverges to -inf or +inf.

Because real data often contains exact 0 and 1, logit() takes an eps and clamps p to [eps, 1 - eps] before the formula. That turns the infinities into large finite values instead.

Parameters¶

eps (double)

Clamp bound. p is restricted to [eps, 1 - eps] first. Required. Pass a tiny value such as 1e-6 to keep exact 0 / 1 inputs finite; pass 0 to allow +/-inf through.

Returns¶

Series or Series& The real-valued scores. logit_() overwrites the current storage.

Gradient¶

logit() is differentiable:

d/dp logit(p) = 1 / (p * (1 - p))

The derivative is smallest (4) at p = 0.5 and grows without bound as p approaches either end. A tracked logit() on probabilities near 0 or 1 therefore produces very large sensitivities.

Examples¶

Example 1. Symmetric probabilities map to symmetric scores.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9}).logit(1e-7));

Output¶

Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[-2.1972, -1.0986, 0.0000, 1.0986, 2.1972]

logit(0.5) = 0, and logit(0.25) = -logit(0.75).

Example 2. eps keeps exact 0 and 1 finite by clamping first.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({0.0, 1.0}).logit(1e-6));

Output¶

Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[-13.8155, 13.8155]

A smaller eps pushes those values further out — logit(0.0) with eps = 1e-12 is about -27.6.

Example 3. The backward is 1 / (p * (1 - p)) — minimal at p = 0.5.

auto p = pluss::make_series({0.2, 0.5, 0.8});
p.tracks_slope_(true);

p.logit(1e-9).sum().reverse();

pluss::series::print(std::cout, p.sensitivity());

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[6.2500, 4.0000, 6.2500]

1 / (0.5 * 0.5) = 4 at the center; 1 / (0.2 * 0.8) = 6.25 on either side.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • eps has no default. Choose it deliberately: too large distorts scores near the ends, too small (or 0) lets +/-inf through.

  • Inputs outside (0, 1) are clamped to [eps, 1 - eps]; logit() does not reject them.

  • The gradient blows up near p = 0 and p = 1.

Summary¶

logit(p, eps) is the inverse sigmoid log(p / (1 - p)):

  • clamps p to [eps, 1 - eps] first; eps is required

  • antisymmetric about p = 0.5, where it is 0

  • differentiable, backward 1 / (p * (1 - p)), unbounded at the ends

See Also¶

  • Series::sigmoid: the forward map logit() inverts.

  • Series::log: the logarithm in the definition.

  • Series::clamp_min / Series::clamp_max: the clamping eps performs, done explicitly.
